summary: Albemarle County tower on Heards Mountain, erected by crews of CCC Camp Albemarle; listed as gone, with no removal date or remains found.

facts.design: steel fire tower similar to the 80-foot one on Carter's Mountain
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no removal date found

events.note: The Crozet Gazette places Camp Albemarle's first tower work in its first six months in 1933 and says the crews erected similar towers on Heards Mountain. Neither source dates the Heards tower separately, so 1933 is the camp's first-year context, not a build record.

evidence.supports: CCC Camp Albemarle at White Hall, established 1933 and disbanded 1942
evidence.quote: Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) Camp Albemarle was established in 1933 at White Hall in western Albemarle County, and operated from that location until it was disbanded in 1942.

evidence.supports: camp's engineer J. Harvey Bailey and its fire-suppression work
evidence.quote: White Hall was one of the several camps who worked especially on suppression of forest fire.

evidence.supports: crews erected similar towers on Heards Mountain
evidence.quote: They erected similar towers on Heards Mountain in southern Albemarle

evidence.quote: They constructed similar towers on Heards Mountain in southern Albemarle

sources.title: Secrets of the Blue Ridge: We Can Take It! Camp Albemarle Civilian Conservation Corps

notes_for_editor: Brief's record checks out: Albemarle County, coordinates and gone status all match the FFLA list. Only two secondary sources describe the Heards tower, each in a sentence or two (the Gazette and Cvillepedia repeat the same CCC account). The tower is not dated; the 1933 event year rests on the Gazette and Cvillepedia both placing the similar towers in the camp's first six months. No height, staffing, access or removal information found; one search returned an alternate spelling 'Heard Mountain' but nothing usable, and the AnyPlaceAmerica page returned 403. No photos. Cvillepedia's 'Carter Mountain' spelling is the Gazette's 'Carter's Mountain'.
